title: The Impact of Financial Reporting Quality on Debt Contracting: Evidence from Internal Control Weakness Reports

models.model_label: Financial covenant count — primary full-sample specification
models.sample_description: Syndicated loan facilities issued to firms reporting material internal control weaknesses in one of three windows: prior (three years before the first ICW report), uncorrected (from first report through first clean report), or corrected (three years after correction). The facility-level sample requires at least one facility before the report and at least one facility in an uncorrected or corrected period, and nonmissing DealScan and Compustat data for loan and firm controls.
models.method_details: The authors describe a regression and print a linear specification, but do not identify the estimator.
models.equation_text: Financial Covenants = α + β 1 Uncorrected + β 2 Corrected + β 3 Institutional Investor + β 4 Revolver + β 5 Interest Rate + β 6 Secured + β 7 Loan Size + β 8 Maturity + β 9 Credit Rating + β 10 Number Lenders + β 11 PP Indicator + β 12 Firm Size + β 13 Profitability + β 14 Leverage + ε

fixed_effects.details: Year fixed effects for loan-year observations.

evidence.quote: Year fixed effects Yes

standard_errors.details: Heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors clustered at the firm level.

evidence.quote: standard errors are heteroskedasticity robust, clustered at the firm level
Contractual term = α + β 1 Uncorrected + β 2 Corrected + βi ( Controli ) , (1)

estimation_procedure.description: Within-sample temporal comparison of loan terms for ICW firms across prior, uncorrected, and corrected periods; the prior period is the reference category. This is a comparison across facility issuance windows, not a reported firm fixed effect.

evidence.quote: We focus on temporal changes in debt contractual terms for firms reporting an ICW
The prior period spans the three years before the ICW was first reported.
Contractual term = α + β 1 Uncorrected + β 2 Corrected + βi ( Controli ) , (1)

missing_fields.method: The paper describes a regression but does not name the underlying estimator for this model; it is left unknown.

dependent_variable.name: Financial Covenants
dependent_variable.definition: Number of financial covenants imposed by the loan agreement.

evidence.quote: Financial Covenants: The number of financial covenants imposed by the loan agreement.

independent_variables.name: Uncorrected
independent_variables.definition: Indicator equal to one for a loan issued while a material internal control weakness is uncorrected; this period runs from the first material weakness through the first report showing that it has been corrected.

evidence.quote: Uncorrected: An indicator variable equal to one if the loan is issued during a period of an uncorrected material internal control weakness. We define this period from the day of the first material internal control weakness through the day of the first report where the weakness has been corrected.

independent_variables.name: Corrected
independent_variables.definition: Indicator equal to one for a loan issued during the three-year period after a material internal control weakness is corrected.
independent_variables.formula: 1 during three years after correction; 0 otherwise.

evidence.quote: Corrected: An indicator variable taking the value of one if the loan is issued in the three-year period following a corrected material internal control weakness, zero otherwise.

independent_variables.name: Institutional Investor
independent_variables.definition: Indicator equal to one when the loan type is term loan B, C, or D (institutional term loans), zero otherwise.

evidence.quote: Institutional Investor: An indicator variable taking the value of one if the loan’s type is term loan B, C, or D (institutional term loans), zero otherwise.

independent_variables.name: Revolver
independent_variables.definition: Indicator equal to one if the loan type is revolver, zero otherwise.

evidence.quote: Revolver: An indicator variable taking the value of one if the loan’s type is revolver, zero otherwise.

independent_variables.name: Interest Rate
independent_variables.definition: DealScan All-in-Drawn-Spread, in basis points over LIBOR per dollar drawn, including the loan spread and annual fee paid to the bank group.

evidence.quote: Interest Rate: The interest rate is based on the All-in-Drawn-Spread measure reported by DealScan. This measure is equal to the amount the borrower pays in basis points over LIBOR for each dollar drawn down, so it accounts for both the spread of the loan and the annual fee paid to the bank group. LPC always uses the LIBOR spread or the LIBORequivalent spread option to calculate the All-in-Drawn spread.

independent_variables.name: Secured
independent_variables.definition: Indicator equal to one if the loan is backed by collateral, zero otherwise.

evidence.quote: Secured: An indicator variable taking the value of one if the loan is backed by collateral, zero otherwise.

independent_variables.name: Loan Size
independent_variables.definition: Logarithm of the loan amount.

evidence.quote: Loan Size: A logarithm of the loan’s amount.

independent_variables.name: Maturity
independent_variables.definition: Months between the facility issue date and maturity date.
independent_variables.formula: months between facility issue and maturity

evidence.quote: Maturity: The number of months between the facility’s issue date and the date when the loan matures.

independent_variables.name: Credit Rating
independent_variables.definition: Numerical senior debt rating: 1 is the highest rating through 27 the lowest; unrated firms are assigned 28. The authors use S&P, Moody’s, Fitch, or DPR in a stated fallback sequence and conventional conversion scheme.

evidence.quote: Credit Rating: The numerical equivalent of S&P, Moody’s, Fitch, or DPR senior debt rating. It is set as equal to 1 for the highest senior debt rating, through 27 for the lowest senior debt rating. For firms not rated by S&P, we assign the Moody’s senior debt rating; for firms not rated by either S&P or Moody’s, we assign the Fitch senior debt rating; finally, for firms not rated by S&P, Moody’s, or Fitch, we assign the DPR senior debt rating. We use a conventional conversion scheme to match ratings from all four rating agencies. The corporate credit rating variable is set to 28 for firms without an available S&P, Moody’s, Fitch, or DPR debt rating. Credit ratings are collected from the S&P Historical Rating Database and from the Mergent FISD database. Financial Covenants: The number of financial covenants imposed by the loan agreement.

independent_variables.name: Number Lenders
independent_variables.definition: Number of participants in the loan syndicate, including the arranger.

evidence.quote: Number Lenders: Number of participants in the loan syndicate, including the arranger.

independent_variables.name: PP Indicator
independent_variables.definition: Indicator equal to one if the loan contract incorporates a performance pricing option, zero otherwise.

evidence.quote: PP Indicator: An indicator variable taking the value of one if the loan contract incorporates a performance pricing option, zero otherwise.

independent_variables.name: Firm Size
independent_variables.definition: Logarithm of the borrower’s total assets in the year before the loan contract.
independent_variables.formula: ln(borrower total assets in prior year)

evidence.quote: Firm Size: A logarithm of the borrower’s total assets in the year prior to entering into a loan contract.

independent_variables.name: Profitability
independent_variables.definition: EBITDA divided by total assets, measured in the year before entering into the loan contract.

evidence.quote: Profitability: The ratio of EBITDA to total assets, estimated in the year prior to entering into a loan contract.

independent_variables.name: Leverage
independent_variables.definition: Long-term debt divided by total assets, measured in the year before entering into the loan contract.

evidence.quote: Leverage: The ratio of the long-term debt to total assets, estimated in the year prior to entering into a loan contract.

result_sets.label: Table 3, column (1): Financial Covenants
result_sets.period: DealScan facilities issued September 1999 through December 2008; loan observations classified as prior, uncorrected, or corrected relative to the material internal control weakness report.
result_sets.population: Final full sample of 2,828 facilities issued to 788 borrowers. Firms have at least one facility before the ICW report and at least one facility in an uncorrected or corrected period.

sample_extraction.data_section_full_text:
3.1 DATA SOURCES AND SAMPLE SELECTION


We obtain data on ICW reports filed under Sarbanes-Oxley Section 302
from Audit Analytics. Section 302 refers to the “Corporate Responsibility
for Financial Reports” and requires that chief executive officers and chief
financial officers evaluate the design and effectiveness of internal controls
and report their overall conclusions on a quarterly basis. Any company filing periodic reports under Sections 13(a) or 15(d) of the Exchange Act,
without exception for firm size, must comply with the rule.

Our initial sample consists of 2,231 firms reporting material weaknesses
over the September 2002 through July 2008 period (table 1). We match
our ICW sample to public firms in the DealScan database and retain all
loans issued in the prior, uncorrected or corrected periods. DealScan is
provided by Loan Pricing Corporation (LPC) and contains a wide range of
loan characteristics, such as interest rate, amount, and covenants. Matching
Audit Analytics to DealScan leads to a sample of 3,666 loans. Furthermore,
we eliminate loans (facilities <sup>8</sup> ) missing the loan or firm characteristics required for the empirical analysis. To ensure that our results are not due to
changes in the sample’s composition, we require the firm to have at least
one loan issued in the prior period and at least one loan issued in either the
uncorrected or corrected periods. Our final sample includes 2,828 facilities
issued to 788 borrowers. <sup>9</sup>

7 A decrease in financial reporting quality can also decrease lenders’ reliance on borrowing base restrictions (so-called asset-based lending). Borrowing base restrictions are typically
found in revolvers to speculative-grade borrowers (LSTA [2007], Standard & Poor’s [2007]).
These restrictions define a maximum borrowing limit tied to a formula primarily based on a
borrower’s inventory and receivables. Because only 13% of our sample loans are subject to a
borrowing base restriction, we do not analyze these restrictions in this study.

8 In the syndicated loan market, a loan is referred to as a “facility.” Usually, a number of
facilities with different maturities, interest rate spreads, and repayment schedules are structured and syndicated as one transaction (deal) with a borrower. The analysis in this paper is
performed at the individual facility level.
